consumptionBoundary.decision: Vinaya consumes Atta's packed public runtime through its injected-executor seam. This is fixed; the matrix decides fit or a named gap against it and selects no other packaging, runtime, orchestration framework or provider-specific core.

rows.capability: Flow and Plan representation and validation
rows.mechanism: A steps-shaped Flow is compiled and validated by @atta/engine into a Plan; the packed consumer compiles one using nothing but supported exports of the installed tarballs.
rows.limitation: The Plan names roles and actions only, and what each resolves to is the consumer's. The checkpoint stores state, never the Plan, so a resume must be handed the same Plan the run started with; the runtime refuses only a Plan that could not have produced the recorded results.

citations.anchor: L160-L176 — 1. A steps-shaped Flow compiles through the installed engine
L67-L75 — What a caller still owns

rows.capability: Packed public runtime consumable outside the Atta workspace
rows.mechanism: The external-consumer proof builds the three packages, packs them, installs only the tarballs into a project verified to sit outside the checkout, typechecks the consumer under strict settings against the installed declarations, and runs the whole run lifecycle there.
rows.limitation: Every packed manifest must be marked private and nothing is published to a registry; the consumer pins the two transitive @atta ranges to the tarballs through overrides. Vinaya therefore installs tarballs built from a recorded Atta commit, not a registry version.

citations.anchor: L1-L42 — stages build, pack, install, typecheck, run
L168-L170 — packed manifest must be private
L217-L245 — consumer overrides pin the transitive @atta ranges

rows.untracedReason: Packaging is a property of the Atta artifacts; the standalone loop's invariant register has no packaging behavior to trace to.

rows.mechanism: buildAgentSpawnStateGraph compiles the Plan with a caller-supplied AgentLifecycleNodeExecutor; the packed consumer drives the graph with its own executor. createAgentLifecycleNodeExecutor is the package's default executor, which a consumer may wrap.
rows.limitation: The executor is one function per node over the package's graph state (runId, results, sessions, revisionCounts). Vinaya's node contracts must be expressed through that state plus Vinaya's own prepared inputs; the halt handle and the resumed-from checkpoint are per-leg options, not run configuration.

citations.anchor: L177-L209 — 2. The consumer injects its own AgentLifecycleNodeExecutor

rows.mechanism: Fan-out and join follow from the Plan's declared edges in the compiled graph: a node with several incoming edges runs once, after all of them; a branch failure rejects the leg's invoke with the join never started.
rows.limitation: A failed branch rejects the whole leg. The cited source does not state what becomes of a sibling branch still running at that moment, so sibling clean-up stays with Vinaya's executor and the reviewer clean-up defect is not closed by the runtime.

rows.mechanism: A caller-supplied BaseCheckpointSaver turns on one checkpoint write per node boundary carrying the whole graph state; readRunCheckpoint reads a suspended run back through that same saver, with no second store beside it.
rows.limitation: The saver, its retention, encryption and access are the caller's choice. Persisted results are narrowed and redacted, which is a floor and not a proof that no secret is stored.

citations.anchor: L199-L259 — AgentSpawnGraphCompileOptions: the only durable-state seam

rows.mechanism: createRunControl().halt stops a leg at the next node boundary; resumeControlledRun continues the same run identity from its own last checkpoint, running only the thread's pending nodes and never a completed one.
rows.limitation: Two concurrent legs of one run both pass their preconditions; serialising legs is the caller's stated obligation, which Vinaya's one-driver-per-task lock has to keep meeting. A node already running when the halt fires reports failed, the leg reports paused, and that node runs again on resume.

citations.anchor: L27-L66 — The three operations; One leg at a time is the caller's obligation
L273-L303 — 5. Resume continues the same run rather than replaying it

rows.mechanism: A halted leg returns a typed paused outcome with its checkpoint and halt reason; resume invokes the graph with no input value, so the decision a human records reaches the resumed node through Vinaya's prepared inputs, read by the injected executor.
rows.limitation: No interrupt-with-value resume is exported at the pinned commit. The decision payload, its authentication and its single consumption stay Vinaya-owned.

citations.anchor: L27-L42 — resume invokes the graph with a null input

rows.mechanism: onEvent receives node:start, node:streaming, node:complete and node:failed, each carrying runId, from one emission point in the executor and in the order they occur.
rows.limitation: Event text is a redacted, bounded excerpt. A consumer needing the verbatim stream reads it from executeAgentSpawnNode's own return value, so Log production reads from Vinaya's executor rather than from onEvent.

citations.anchor: L89-L122 — onEvent: what arrives here is redacted
L210-L252 — 3. Durable start, live observation, halt at a node boundary

rows.mechanism: Cancellation reaches a node already running: the spawned process receives the graceful termination signal, then the forced one after a bounded wait, and the node fails with ProcessCancelledError.
rows.limitation: It terminates processes the executor spawned during this process's lifetime. A child left behind by a dead driver is not tracked by the runtime, so orphan reaping across a driver death stays with the adapter and Vinaya.

citations.anchor: L304-L330 — 6. Cancellation terminates a node already running

rows.mechanism: startControlledRun and resumeControlledRun return a RunOutcome discriminated on reason (completed, paused, failed, exhausted); readRunOutcome reads the recorded outcome back from the checkpointer.
rows.limitation: These are runtime outcomes, not Vinaya's terminal meanings; there is no cancelled outcome reason, so Vinaya maps its five terminal outcomes onto them explicitly.

citations.anchor: Errors are part of the flow

rows.mechanism: A Plan names a role or an action; the executor resolves it only through the consumer's roleBinaries and mechanicalActions, checks the step's permission against the role's non-empty allowedPermissions, and refuses anything undeclared.
rows.limitation: Permission values are the consumer's vocabulary; the runtime enforces membership in the list, not what a value means to the spawned CLI.

citations.anchor: L331-L350 — 7. Bounds — the executor refuses what the consumer never declared

rows.capability: Subscription-login invocation with an environment allowlist
rows.mechanism: RoleBinaryConfig never carries a vendor API key: the spawned CLI authenticates through its own logged-in session, buildArgs is the caller's, and the spawned environment is an allowlist (PATH and HOME by default) plus the role's own named variables; every working directory must resolve inside workingDirectoryRoot.
rows.limitation: The runtime bounds the working directory and the environment only; OS confinement of the spawned CLI is the provider adapter's.

citations.anchor: L30-L59 — RoleBinaryConfig: never a vendor API key
3. Mechanism, host capabilities, authentication path and refusal conditions

rows.untracedReason: Subscription-only authentication is a Principal ruling recorded in the isolation spec, not a standalone-loop behavior in the invariant register.

rows.capability: Redaction of observed and persisted agent output
rows.mechanism: One redaction pass at the single emission point for observers, and a narrowing pass over every result written into the checkpoint, each marking which fields it narrowed.
rows.limitation: Only recognised shapes are replaced, so this is a floor rather than a proof; retained excerpts are still agent-derived.

citations.anchor: L223-L256 — what supplying a checkpointer actually persists
L351-L374 — 8. Observer text and persisted results are redacted and bounded

rows.untracedReason: The standalone loop persists no agent output into a checkpoint, so its invariant register has no redaction behavior to trace to.

rows.mechanism: The external consumer installs only @atta/agents, @atta/engine and @atta/executor-agent-spawn, and asserts that @atta/adapter-langgraph is not installed at all.
rows.limitation: A capability only the rounds-shaped adapter offers is outside the consumption boundary by construction and cannot be assumed.

citations.anchor: L375-L398 — 9. The rounds-shaped adapter is absent, not merely unimported

rows.untracedReason: Packaging fact about the Atta artifact set; the invariant register has no packaging behavior to trace to.

rows.mechanism: Vinaya's injected executor and control state decide every next step and every terminal meaning; the graph only executes the edges the Plan declares.
rows.limitation: The runtime's outcome reasons are coarser than Vinaya's five terminal outcomes, so the mapping stays explicit and Vinaya-owned.

rows.mechanism: Reviewer verdicts are validated against one review-input manifest, and convergence exits are decided by Vinaya's assessment over held verdicts and objectives.
rows.limitation: The runtime's own revision ceiling (its exhausted outcome) is not the convergence rule; Vinaya's round cap and exit order stay authoritative, and the open defect publishing on an empty verdict set is Vinaya's to fix.

rows.mechanism: Round cap, time budget and retry bounds are Vinaya configuration checked by Vinaya's nodes; the runtime contributes per-role process timeouts and a recursion limit forwarded to invoke.
rows.limitation: A role's process timeout defaults to ten minutes in the runtime; Vinaya must set it from its own budgets rather than inherit the default.

rows.mechanism: Push, pull-request open and verdict publication go through Vinaya's effect executor, prepared, committed and reconciled by a stable identity, so a node that runs again reconciles instead of repeating.
rows.limitation: Resume re-runs a node that was in flight at the halt and the runtime keeps no effect ledger, so every effect inside a node must be keyed and reconcilable.

citations.anchor: L43-L66 — no transcript replay; legs serialised by the caller

rows.mechanism: Task start, status, escalation read, resume and cancel map onto the run-control port and Vinaya's escalation and resolution records.
rows.limitation: Resume authentication by ruling ordinal and the single claim of a resolution are Vinaya-owned; the open defects there are not changed by the runtime.

citations.anchor: Human handoff is durable, not an error string

rows.mechanism: Vinaya emits every loop event from its own nodes into its typed Log families under one run identity; the runtime's events are an observation input, never the Log.
rows.limitation: Runtime event text is a redacted excerpt, and Log events built from it inherit that redaction.

citations.anchor: L89-L122 — onEvent: what arrives here is redacted

rows.mechanism: The brief, objectives, rulings, pull-request facts and review-input manifest are prepared once by Vinaya and delivered to a node by the injected executor.
rows.limitation: The checkpoint stores graph state only, so prepared inputs carry their own versions for a resumed node to read the same ones or detect the change.

citations.anchor: L67-L75 — What a caller still owns

rows.mechanism: One agent invocation is started, resumed, cancelled and observed through this port with no vendor format in its signature; each adapter implements it behind the port, inside the injected executor.
rows.limitation: Every adapter supplies every required adapter capability; one an adapter cannot document is a named gap, never assumed present.

citations.anchor: L22-L23 — executeAgentSpawnNode and the SpawnFn seam

rows.capability: ToolCatalog: list by role and phase, invoke with authority
rows.mechanism: Tools are listed per role and phase and invoked with the caller's granted authority; the catalog's driver side, not the agent, holds the forge credential and runs the governed operation.
rows.limitation: Tool authority currently rests on which process can reach the tool server, which the same-user socket gap names.

rows.mechanism: Sources are prepared once per round under stable identities and delivered to a node; the port says what is delivered, never how a given runtime receives it.
rows.limitation: Delivery into a worker is by prompt and staged files, translated by the adapter.

rows.mechanism: Every external effect is prepared with a stable identity, committed once, and reconciled against the remote when its outcome is uncertain.
rows.limitation: Reconciliation needs the remote to expose the effect's identity; an effect without one cannot be made effect-once.

rows.capability: RunControl: start, inspect, halt, resume, cancel, stream
rows.mechanism: Start maps to startControlledRun, inspect to readRunCheckpoint and readRunOutcome, halt to createRunControl().halt, resume to resumeControlledRun, cancel to the halt signal reaching a live child, and stream to onEvent.
rows.limitation: In the runtime, cancel is a halt plus live-child termination; fencing in-flight effects to uncertain is Vinaya's.

citations.anchor: L35-L51 — run-control, run-halt and run-identity exports

rows.capability: One node contract for every adapter
rows.mechanism: Every node carries typed input, typed output, side-effect class, retry, timeout, failure and cancellation behavior and its owned Log events; no field names a vendor, a model, a hook, a tool-block format or a session format.
rows.limitation: A vendor-specific capability may appear only in an adapter-owned cell; a need that cannot be expressed through the five ports is escalated, never added as a core field.

rows.mechanism: The developer gets repository exploration, edit and test plus brokered branch and pull-request operations; reviewers get reads and one bounded result channel; the Operator gets task start, status, escalation, resume and cancel.
rows.limitation: Grants are enforced by the tool catalog and by each adapter's permission translation; worker-side lifecycle hooks are never the guarantee.

rows.mechanism: Adapters are coding-agent CLIs under subscription login: no paid provider API, no API key and no hosted graph service.
rows.limitation: The vendor documents API-key routes for minimal and automation runs; those routes are excluded, and an adapter that cannot run under subscription login refuses.

citations.anchor: 3. Mechanism, host capabilities, authentication path and refusal conditions
L30-L59 — RoleBinaryConfig: never a vendor API key

rows.untracedReason: Subscription-only authentication is a Principal ruling recorded in the isolation spec, not a standalone-loop behavior in the invariant register.

rows.mechanism: Vinaya's code, not a model, selects every next step over typed observations; model output is an input to that choice.
rows.limitation: Pattern classification only: the agents-SDK guide describes an API-key SDK and grounds no adapter cell.

citations.anchor: When (and when not) to use agents

rows.mechanism: The developer produces a candidate, reviewers evaluate it against frozen objectives, and findings return to the same developer session until the evaluation passes or an exit applies.
rows.limitation: The pattern fits only with clear evaluation criteria; without frozen objectives the cycle has nothing to converge on.

rows.mechanism: One run identity spans every node event as a trace spans its spans, and sensitive payloads are excluded or redacted before they are stored.
rows.limitation: Pattern classification only: Vinaya's Log families and the runtime's runId are the implementation, not the agents-SDK tracing.

rows.mechanism: Driver-run tools consolidate one governed multi-step operation into a single call that returns a success or a structured refusal the agent can act on.
rows.limitation: Tool descriptions steer an agent; they enforce nothing, so enforcement stays in the driver behind each tool.

rows.mechanism: claude -p runs one prompt non-interactively with the flags the adapter passes, exiting 0 on success and non-zero when the run fails.
rows.limitation: Without --bare a -p run loads the working directory's hooks and MCP servers; --bare never reads the subscription login, so it is unusable under subscription-only auth.

rows.mechanism: --output-format json with --json-schema returns the schema-conforming result in structured_output alongside session id and usage metadata.
rows.limitation: The format keyword is accepted as an annotation and not enforced.

rows.mechanism: --output-format stream-json --verbose emits one JSON event per line, ending with a result message carrying the final text, cost and session metadata.
rows.limitation: A foreground subagent's text is omitted unless --forward-subagent-text is passed.

rows.mechanism: The session id read from json output is passed back with --resume to continue that conversation; --session-id fixes the id up front.
rows.limitation: The system prompt recorded on a conversation's first request is reused on resume until compaction, so changed prompt flags do not apply to a resumed conversation.

citations.anchor: System prompt flags in resumed conversations

rows.mechanism: --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config loads only the named servers; the system/init event reports mcp_servers and mcp_server_errors.
rows.limitation: An entry failing validation is skipped and the run continues, so the adapter fails the dispatch on a non-empty mcp_server_errors.

citations.anchor: Fail CI when a plugin or MCP server doesn't load

rows.mechanism: --tools restricts built-in tools, --allowedTools and --disallowedTools carry allow and deny rules, and --settings supplies a per-dispatch settings file.
rows.limitation: Allow rules approve calls; they do not confine what a call reaches, which is the sandbox row's job.

rows.mechanism: --permission-prompts none denies anything that would prompt unless a rule or PermissionRequest hook resolves it, and removes tools that need a person.
rows.limitation: The flag requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later; earlier versions reject it.

citations.anchor: Turn off permission prompts in unattended runs

rows.mechanism: SIGTERM ends the run with exit 143, terminates running Bash process trees and runs SessionEnd hooks; SIGINT ends the turn instead.
rows.limitation: The interrupted turn records no result; a resume continues from the next prompt unless CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1 is set.

rows.mechanism: json output carries usage, total_cost_usd and a per-model cost breakdown.
rows.limitation: Cost figures are client-side estimates and accumulate across resumed runs of one conversation.

rows.mechanism: A non-zero exit marks failure, an in-run failure is printed as the result, and system/api_retry events name an error category (authentication_failed, rate_limit, overloaded and others).
rows.limitation: Categories are vendor vocabulary; the adapter maps them onto the core's normalized error kinds and treats unknown ones as unknown.

rows.mechanism: --append-system-prompt-file and --model set role instructions and model; subagents defined with --agents run in their own context window with their own tool list and model.
rows.limitation: Subagent definitions are adapter configuration; the core names roles, never subagents.

rows.mechanism: Hooks configured in a settings file fire on lifecycle events; a PreToolUse hook can deny a call and a Stop hook exiting 2 keeps the session going.
rows.limitation: Hooks run outside the sandbox with the session's environment; they are an adapter mechanism and never a product guarantee.

rows.mechanism: codex exec runs one prompt non-interactively; it runs in a read-only sandbox unless a sandbox mode is given.
rows.limitation: The cited sections state no exit-status contract, so the adapter reads the final turn event rather than the exit code alone.

rows.mechanism: --output-schema takes a JSON Schema file and the final response conforms to it; -o writes it to a file.
rows.limitation: The schema is a file path, so the adapter stages it inside the task's scratch.

citations.anchor: Create structured outputs with a schema

rows.mechanism: --json turns stdout into JSON Lines: thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed, turn.failed, item.* and error events.
rows.limitation: Item shapes are vendor vocabulary translated by the adapter.

rows.mechanism: codex exec resume <SESSION_ID> continues a recorded session (or --last the most recent).
rows.limitation: A resumed run accepts no sandbox flag, so the sandbox and network policy must come from the task-scoped CODEX_HOME config read by both fresh and resumed runs.

citations.anchor: 4b. Codex's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.mechanism: [mcp_servers.<name>] tables in config.toml register STDIO or streamable HTTP servers, with startup_timeout_sec and tool_timeout_sec.
rows.limitation: Registration is per CODEX_HOME, so the adapter stages a task-scoped home rather than reading the operator's.

rows.mechanism: enabled_tools allowlists and disabled_tools denylists a server's tools; the sandbox mode and approval policy bound what commands may do.
rows.limitation: Tool lists are per server; built-in command execution is bounded by the sandbox mode, not by a per-tool list.

rows.mechanism: The sandbox mode decides what runs and the approval policy decides when to pause; unattended runs use workspace-write.
rows.limitation: danger-full-access removes the filesystem and network boundary and is never used for an unattended dispatch.

rows.mechanism: The runtime's executor terminates the spawned codex exec process with the graceful, then the forced, signal.
rows.limitation: The cited Codex sections document no interrupt or cancellation semantics for codex exec, nor what a resumed session holds for an interrupted turn; this is not assumed present.

rows.mechanism: turn.completed carries usage: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens and output_tokens.
rows.limitation: Token counts only; no cost figure is reported.

rows.mechanism: turn.failed and error events report a failed turn and a run-level error on the JSON Lines stream.
rows.limitation: The cited section enumerates no error vocabulary, so the adapter maps what it recognises and normalizes the rest to an unknown kind.

rows.mechanism: Role context is the prompt plus the task-scoped configuration; --ignore-user-config and --ignore-rules keep the operator's own configuration out of an automated run.
rows.limitation: No subagent-definition mechanism appears in the cited sections; role context is the prompt and the scoped home only.

rows.mechanism: Inside a writable root, .git, .agents and .codex stay read-only.
rows.limitation: The driver grants the linked worktree's git common dir writable, widening that protection for the task's own repository (accepted in the isolation spec).

citations.anchor: 4b. Codex's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.sandbox: Claude Code's built-in sandbox, enforced with Seatbelt
rows.mechanism: The driver writes a sandbox block into the per-dispatch --settings file: writes limited to the worktree, scratch and bun's install cache; named credential files and the driver-tool socket root denied to reads; a strict domain allowlist; no excluded commands.
rows.refusal: The sandbox block sets failIfUnavailable and turns the unsandboxed retry off, so a sandbox that cannot start ends the run instead of running unsandboxed; an unattended dispatch whose settings file cannot be written refuses before spawn.
rows.publication: publish_changes, open_pull_request, update_pull_request_body, refresh_evidence, read_pull_request and run_checks run in the driver outside the sandbox; gh and git push are denied to the worker.
rows.limitation: Only tool calls are confined: the Claude Code main process, its hooks and its local MCP servers run outside the sandbox, and reads stay open except the named credential files and the socket root.

citations.anchor: 4a. Claude's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row
2. Existing precedent this contract extends, not invents

rows.sandbox: Claude Code's built-in sandbox, enforced with bubblewrap and a socat-bridged egress proxy
rows.mechanism: The same sandbox block as on macOS, enforced by bubblewrap with egress bridged through socat.
rows.refusal: An unattended dispatch refuses before spawn when bwrap or socat does not resolve on PATH, writing a WARNING lifecycle line and an operation event with result unavailable; failIfUnavailable ends a run whose sandbox fails to start.
rows.publication: publish_changes, open_pull_request, update_pull_request_body, refresh_evidence, read_pull_request and run_checks run in the driver outside the sandbox; gh and git push are denied to the worker.
rows.limitation: The Unix-socket seccomp filter is optional, so the socket-root read deny is what hides sibling sockets; bubblewrap needs user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 and later restrict by default.

citations.anchor: 4a. Claude's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.sandbox: Codex's workspace-write sandbox, enforced with Seatbelt (sandbox-exec), plus its network proxy
rows.mechanism: A config.toml staged into a task-scoped CODEX_HOME sets workspace-write and the network-proxy domain allowlist; the worktree, scratch, bun's install cache and the linked worktree's git common dir are the writable roots.
rows.refusal: resolveCodexConfinement returns a refusal, never a degraded unconfined launch, when the sandbox, its network proxy or the staged CODEX_HOME is unavailable; a staging or auth-preflight failure refuses the same way, before spawn.
rows.publication: publish_changes, open_pull_request, update_pull_request_body, refresh_evidence, read_pull_request and run_checks run in the driver outside the sandbox; the worker holds no forge credential.
rows.limitation: workspace-write has no read restriction, so reads reach anything the user can read; the network proxy does not filter MCP server connections.

citations.anchor: 4b. Codex's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.sandbox: Codex's workspace-write sandbox, enforced with bwrap and seccomp, plus its own network proxy
rows.mechanism: The same staged config.toml as on macOS; Codex runs its own local proxy, so bwrap is the only host tool required.
rows.refusal: An unattended dispatch refuses before spawn when bwrap is not on PATH; the refusal names the missing tool.
rows.publication: publish_changes, open_pull_request, update_pull_request_body, refresh_evidence, read_pull_request and run_checks run in the driver outside the sandbox; the worker holds no forge credential.
rows.limitation: workspace-write has no read restriction, and the network proxy does not filter MCP server connections.

citations.anchor: 4b. Codex's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.capability: Driver-run code executes outside the sandbox
rows.owningLayer: Vinaya driver: governed effects and the driver-run tools
rows.mechanism: Publication, pull-request reads and checks run with the forge credential in the driver's own unconfined process; the agent CLI's hooks and local MCP servers also run with the user's full access.
rows.limitation: Driver-run work that executes repository content the worker wrote, such as the repository's commit and push hooks during publish_changes or the checks run_checks executes, runs with the driver's authority and outside any sandbox.

rows.capability: Tool-socket reach between processes of the same user
rows.owningLayer: Vinaya tool catalog: the driver-run tools server
rows.mechanism: Each task's driver-run tools listen on a socket; confinement hides the socket root from sandboxed tool calls only.
rows.limitation: Any unconfined process of the same user, including an agent CLI's own main process, its hooks and MCP servers, can reach another task's socket; the isolation spec closes this only by confining the worker and names no per-caller check on the socket.

citations.anchor: 4a. Claude's own mechanism — the six boundaries, per row

rows.owningLayer: Codex provider adapter: session and credential staging
rows.mechanism: An unattended Codex dispatch copies the operator's auth.json into the task-scoped CODEX_HOME so the confined session authenticates.
rows.limitation: The copy is a durable bearer token readable by any repository command the confined Codex runs, and can leave over allowed egress; workspace-write has no read restriction to stop it.
